The words

Let all mortal flesh keep silence,
And with fear and trembling stand;
Ponder nothing earthly minded,
For with blessing in His hand,
Christ our God to earth descendeth,
Our full homage to demand.

King of kings, yet born of Mary,
As of old on earth He stood,
Lord of lords, in human vesture,
In the body and the blood;
He will give to all the faithful
His own self for heav'nly food.

Rank on rank the host of heaven
Spreads its vanguard on the way,
As the Light of light descendeth
From the realms of endless day,
That the pow'rs of hell may vanish
As the darkness clears away.

At His feet the six wingèd seraph,
Cherubim with sleepless eye,
Veil their faces to the presence,
As with ceaseless voice they cry:
Alleluia, Alleluia
Alleluia, Lord Most High!

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum F and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on l, (D).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

The words are anonymous, in print by 400. The English translation is by Gerard Moultrie (1864). The tune, PICARDY, is Traditional French. This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.

  • Words (400): From Liturgy of St. James
  • Translated (1864): Gerard Moultrie (1829–1885)
  • Melody: Traditional French

Questions about Let All Mortal Flesh Keep Silence

What is the doh of Let All Mortal Flesh Keep Silence?

In this version, in D minor, doh is F. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Let All Mortal Flesh Keep Silence start on?

It starts on l, (D in D minor). Find doh first, then sing up or down to l,.

Is Let All Mortal Flesh Keep Silence in the public domain?

Yes. Gerard Moultrie died in 1885; the words were first published in 1864 and the music in 1906. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in Nigeria, the UK, the EU and the United States. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
